details:
Lunar Landing Site Navigator is an interactive decision-support platform developed to simplify the evaluation and comparison of potential landing sites in the Moon's south polar region. The project focuses on three candidate locations: Shackleton Crater, Malapert Massif, and the Lunar South Pole.

The platform brings together scientific and engineering information from multiple NASA resources into a single user-friendly interface. Users can explore landing sites, compare their characteristics, define mission timelines, and prioritize mission objectives such as landing safety, water ice availability, solar illumination, and Earth communication visibility.

Using a weighted decision model, the system analyzes mission priorities and calculates the most suitable landing site among the three candidates. It then provides a recommendation supported by site coordinates, terrain characteristics, illumination conditions, communication opportunities, and mission assessment results.

Benefits

  • Simplifies lunar landing site evaluation and comparison.
  • Reduces the time required to analyze information from multiple sources.
  • Supports data-driven mission planning and decision-making.
  • Makes complex scientific information easier to understand and use.
  • Provides a clear recommendation based on mission priorities.

Intended Impact

The project aims to support future lunar exploration missions by helping users identify suitable landing locations efficiently. It demonstrates how NASA open data can be transformed into practical tools that improve mission planning and increase understanding of lunar environments.

NASA Data and Resources Used

  • NASA Moon Trek
  • NASA/JPL Horizons System
  • NASA LROC QuickMap
  • NASA Moon Exploration Program
  • Artemis Program resources

Technologies and Tools Used

  • HTML5
  • CSS3
  • JavaScript
  • Python (Flask)
  • GitHub
  • Canva

Creativity and Innovation

Instead of requiring users to navigate multiple scientific tools and datasets, Lunar Landing Site Navigator combines relevant information into a single interactive platform. The project integrates landing safety, illumination, water ice potential, communication visibility, terrain analysis, mission duration, and user-defined priorities into one decision-making workflow.

Factors Considered

  • Landing safety
  • Water ice availability
  • Solar illumination
  • Earth visibility and communication
  • Terrain slope and elevation
  • Mission timeline and duration
  • User-selected mission priorities

By combining these factors into a unified recommendation system, the project helps simplify lunar mission planning and supports informed landing-site selection for future Moon exploration mission
